newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money dips in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money dips in liquid market.

text.p: Manila overnight money dipped to an average of 11.28125 percent on Friday from 11.3125 due to the high liquidity in the system, traders said.
The market was injected with more liquidity from the maturities of special series Treasury bills since Wednesday, they said.
Done rates were from 11.5 to 11.28125 percent, with 29 lenders and 19 borrowers.
In the secondary market, there was little activity as banks marked their time awaiting the next Treasury bill auction.

Traders said quotes in the secondary market were too low and discouraged banks to buy bills. The lower rates came after the Central Bank dropped its overnight borrowing rate on Thursday by 0.25 percentage points to 11.25 percent.
"We'd rather wait for the auction where prices would be better," a dealer said.
Though a decline in T-bill rates are expected during the auction, the rates are expected to be higher than the secondary market, traders said.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.75/10.90 percent and offers of 10.625 to 10.70 for the three-month bills.
